chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj and Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The mother and the daughter are the same (permissible to marry), if he has not consummated the marriage with her. He means: if a man marries a woman and then divorces her before consummating the marriage, then if he wishes he may marry her mother, and if he wishes he may marry her daughter.
ai.seo_question: Does a man have to marry both the mother and daughter if he divorces one before consummation?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling to clarify that the prohibition of marrying a woman's mother or daughter is contingent upon consummation (dakhala biha); without it, the marital bond is not fully established for the purpose of these specific prohibitions. This distinction is crucial in Shia fiqh for determining whether a man may marry the mother or daughter of his former wife after a pre-consummation divorce, highlighting the legal weight placed on physical union in establishing permanent marital barriers.
